clue.text: Simple to order one about

parts.note: in biology a class is one order of ranking, and the words are interchangeable as a grade or category
the Roman numeral for one
c. is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Something that is easy to request, perhaps a meal ordered for one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple to order' reads as one phrase about ease; 'Simple' alone is the definition, and 'to' just links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic design is plain, timeless and free of fussy ornament, so the adjective can stand for unfussy.

clue.text: Can each change without a promising opportunity?

indicators.note: to change the letters is to rearrange them into a new order
going without something means doing without it, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
this letter is removed once

explanation.surface: Wondering whether each person could change without being handed a good opening.
explanation.walkthrough: One A is dropped from the two words before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance is an opportunity, and the question mark allows for one that looks favourable.

clue.text: Lost man found at the end of a road

parts.note: taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street, a road
Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: A missing person turns up where a road runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found at the end of' puts the man's name after the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To go astray is to wander off the right path and become lost.

clue.text: Firm to have ownership of castle

parts.note: firm and strong both mean solid and robust
to hold property is to own or possess it

explanation.surface: A company taking possession of a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a business noun but supplies an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronghold is a fortified place, and a castle is the classic fortress.

clue.text: Novice soldier acted wrongly

indicators.note: doing something wrongly gets it out of its proper order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A new recruit has behaved badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young trainee in the armed forces, learning to become an officer.

clue.text: Artist has acid thrown over student revolutionary

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

indicators.note: something thrown is tossed about and lands in disorder, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L is the learner plate on a British student driver's car

explanation.surface: A painter flings acid over a firebrand student activist.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-to-earth reading 'over' places the acid on the student; here it simply puts the rearranged letters before L.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical wants sweeping, fundamental change, which is what a revolutionary also seeks.

clue.text: The others are outside school control

indicators.note: one word stands outside the other, wrapping around it

parts.note: the rest are all the others
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: The other pupils are out of the classroom and beyond discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a verb here, not the building.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is the holding back or curbing of something, a form of control.

clue.text: Disaster upset one's state of mind

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means tipped over, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a mood is a temporary state of mind

explanation.surface: A catastrophe has disturbed somebody's mental balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like it describes the person's feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is ruin or terrible fate, a catastrophe.

clue.text: Spice Girl turned up after about one on Monday

parts.note: c. is short for circa, about
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means flipped to read upwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: A member of the Spice Girls pop group showed up early on Monday.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'Spice Girl' as the pop group hides that 'Spice' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnamon is the aromatic bark of a tropical tree, ground or in sticks, used to flavour food.

clue.text: Paid attention to strangely silent journalist

indicators.note: behaving strangely means acting out of the normal order, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ed. is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter who oddly kept quiet and heeded what was said.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who listened gave heed to what was said, the same as paying attention.

clue.text: Change later after going out

indicators.note: letters going out of their usual places end up in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to get changed later, once you've been out for the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to modify or make it different, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Refuses to believe in making savings

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rejects or disregards as untrue

definitions.note: a noun sense: discounts are the savings made on a price
definitions.meaning: second meaning: price reductions that let a shopper save money

explanation.surface: Someone sceptical about whether cutting costs ever really saves anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two halves together as one sceptic's attitude; they are two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means dismisses or disregards a claim; as a plural noun it means reductions in price that save money.

clue.text: Shop with broken china stock

indicators.note: broken crockery is in pieces, and the pieces are put back together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a store is a stock or supply kept for use

explanation.surface: A shop whose stock of china has arrived broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes broken describe damaged stock, but it acts only on china, leaving stock to supply its synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain store is one branch of a retail group with many outlets, so it is a kind of shop.

clue.text: Dull variety of meat

indicators.note: a variety is a different version of something, so the letters come in another form

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint about a bland cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tame is unexciting and lacking spirit, the same sense as dull or flat.

clue.text: Reason gigs deteriorate into violence

indicators.note: things that deteriorate fall apart, and their pieces are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written, every letter to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An explanation for why concerts turn into brawls.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggression is hostile or violent behaviour towards others.

clue.text: Bring her one sort of pattern

indicators.note: to sort things is to rearrange them, so the preceding letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, every letter to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A request to fetch a woman a single item of some kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Herringbone is a zigzag weave or brickwork layout resembling a fish skeleton, so it is a kind of pattern.

clue.text: Right to adapt grade one instrument

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: to adapt is to alter, so the following letters are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: It's correct to arrange a beginner's music exam piece for some instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Grade one is the first music exam a learner takes, which suits the musical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed organ, such as a harmonium, is a keyboard instrument sounded by vibrating metal reeds.

clue.text: Correspondence let spies off

indicators.note: something off is not right, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, every letter to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Letters that allowed secret agents to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistles are letters, especially formal ones, and letters collectively make up correspondence.

clue.text: One who has a telling role

definitions.text: One who has a telling role

parts.words: One who has a telling role
parts.note: surface reading: an actor with a significant, effective part
setter's reading: telling as in telling tales to the authorities

explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling' usually means striking or significant; here it means passing on secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: This person secretly gives the police information about others, so the job is to tell on people.

clue.text: Trick question posed by car worker?

parts.note: setter's reading: a quizmaster who stumps the experts on a game show defeats its board of contestants
surface reading: a mechanic who hammers dented bodywork back into shape

explanation.walkthrough: A game-show panel can be beaten by a trick question; a car body is made of panels that a garage hammers back into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: This tradesman repairs damaged vehicle bodywork by hammering out dents, so he is a motor-trade worker.

clue.text: Colour found fashionable by girl with spirit

parts.note: what is in is fashionable
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
go means energy or spirit, as in full of go

explanation.surface: A shade that a lively young woman has decided is in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet hue, one of the colours of the rainbow.

clue.text: Finished secondary school, reportedly

parts.note: B is the second grade, after A

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: Eton is a famous English private school near Windsor

explanation.surface: Someone has completed their time at secondary school, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is beaten is defeated and done for, so finished in that sense.

clue.text: That's how to hold a demonstration!

indicators.note: the phrase is said to hold something within its letters, spanning the word break

parts.note: the last letter of the first word runs on into the second

explanation.surface: An organiser explaining the proper way to stage a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A show is a display or exhibition put on for others to see, as a demonstration is.

clue.text: Creature meaning wisdom

parts.note: one example of a creature
the sense of a word is its meaning

explanation.surface: The significance some animal is said to symbolise, namely being wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse sense is plain practical good judgment, a homely kind of wisdom.

clue.text: It's divine in the woods!

parts.note: surface reading: an exclamation that a forest walk is lovely
setter's reading: divine as a noun, a minor god who lives in forests

explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like gushing praise but names a deity; the woodland one in Greek myth is half man, half goat.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology this lustful half-goat spirit is a minor woodland god attending Dionysus.

clue.text: Feel awful having to go away

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disarray

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone feels terrible about being forced to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away from danger, a hurried way to leave.

clue.text: Green source of illumination generates publicity

parts.note: lime is a shade of green
a light, such as a lamp, is a source of illumination

explanation.surface: A green lamp somehow attracts attention to itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Limelight was a bright stage lamp, so the surface nearly describes the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the limelight means being the focus of public attention, which is what publicity brings.

clue.text: In beginning I'd to play the fool

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: only the opening letter of this word is used

indicators.note: letters set to play move about freely and settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recalling that at first they had to act the clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play the fool' reads as a single idiom, but 'to play' is the anagram signal and 'the fool' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, the same meaning as a fool.

clue.text: Child harbours desire to be a doctor

indicators.note: a port harbours ships within it, so one word shelters the other inside

parts.note: a son is a male child
an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A youngster secretly wishes to go into medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a medically qualified practitioner who operates, so a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Criticise for being dilapidated

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a phrasal verb for disparaging someone
second meaning: an adjective for shabby and neglected

explanation.surface: Finding fault with a building because it is falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something down is to belittle it; a run-down house is shabby and in poor repair.
